### Siamese network hyperparameter search

<!-- Task 5 (Siamese part): grid search over m, learning rate, filters, and number of epochs trained using validation data to decide on final model. -->

For the Siamese neural network, the margin $m$, learning rate, and batch size were tuned using a grid search, while the CNN encoder architecture and number of epochs were fixed. For each hyperparameter combination, the validation balanced accuracy was calculated at different thresholds, and the threshold that maximised balanced accuracy was selected. However, using the same validation dataset to select the threshold and evaluate balanced accuracy is a limitation. Ideally, the validation data would be divided into two sets, with one used to calculate the threshold from and the other to evaluate balanced accuracy at that threshold. However, because the validation pairs were constructed from only four writers, this dataset was too small to split meaningfully. As with the CNN hyperparameter tuning, a coarse grid search using 36 combinations of hyperparameters (@fig-snn-hpo-coarse) was followed by a refined grid search involving 9 combinations around the best-performing region in the coarse grid (@fig-snn-hpo-refined). 

```{r}
#| label: snn-hpo-cache

snn_hpo_refined_file <- "results/snn_hpo_refined.rds"
```

```{r}
#| label: snn-hpo-define
#| eval: !expr snn_hpo_run_any

# Function to define Siamese network with variable hyperparameters and calculate balanced accuracy from validation data 
build_snn <- function(m, learning_rate, epochs, batch_size) {

  image <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1)) # each image = 28x28, 1 image channel
  
  z <- image |>
    layer_conv_2d(16, kernel_size = c(3,3), activation = "relu") |> # learns useful features (shapes, strokes)
    layer_max_pooling_2d(2) |> # makes feature maps smaller while keeping important info
    layer_conv_2d(32, kernel_size = c(3,3), activation = "relu") |>
    layer_global_average_pooling_2d() |> # converts feature maps -> single vector of numbers
    layer_dense(16) # converts to 16-no embedding representing the handwriting style
  
  encoder <- keras_model(image, z)
  
  
  a <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))
  b <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))
  
  distance <- list(encoder(a), encoder(b)) |>
    layer_lambda(f = function(z) {
      op_sqrt(op_sum(op_square(z[[1]] - z[[2]]), 
                     axis = 2, # sum over embedding dimension
                     keepdims = TRUE) + 
                1e-7) # makes sure it's not 0
    })
  
  model <- keras_model(list(a, b), distance)
  
  contrastive_loss <- function(y, d) {
    op_mean( # finds avg loss across all pairs in a batch
      y * op_square(d) + # squares each pair's distance - for same-writer pairs, penalises a large distance
        (1 - y) * op_square(op_maximum(m - d, 0))) # for diff writer pairs, penalises only if distance is < 1: if dist >=1, penalty is 0
}

  model |> compile(
    optimizer = optimizer_adam(learning_rate = learning_rate),
    loss = contrastive_loss
  )
  
  model |> fit(
    list(train$left, train$right), train$y,
    validation_data = list(
      list(valid$left, valid$right), valid$y
    ),
    epochs = epochs,
    batch_size = batch_size,
    verbose=0
  )
  
  valid_distance <- as.numeric(predict(model, list(valid$left, valid$right), verbose = 0))
  valid_same <- as.logical(valid$y[, 1])
  
  # Function to calculate balanced accuracy at different thresholds
balanced_accuracy_at <- function(cut) {
  predicts_same <- valid_distance < cut # at given threshold (cut) would model predict same or different?
  same_rate <- mean(predicts_same[valid_same]) # accuracy for "same" pairs
  different_rate <- mean(!predicts_same[!valid_same]) # accuracy for "different" pairs
  (same_rate + different_rate) / 2 # mean accuracy for "same" and "different" ("alanced accuracy)
}

  threshold_candidates <- sort(unique(valid_distance))
  threshold_scores <- vapply(threshold_candidates, balanced_accuracy_at, numeric(1))
  best_index <- which.max(threshold_scores)
  threshold <- threshold_candidates[best_index]
  balanced_accuracy <- threshold_scores[best_index]
  
  return(balanced_accuracy)
  
}

# Function to fit multiple iterations of Siamese network from grid of hyperparameters (grid search)
build_snn_grid <- function(grid) {
  
  snn_grid <- list() # initialise list to store results
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(grid)) { # iterate over hyperparameter combinations
    
    set_random_seed(25) # reproducibility
    
    # fit models
    snn <- build_snn(grid$m_values[i], grid$lr_values[i], grid$epochs[i], grid$batch_size[i]) 
    
    # fill list with results
    snn_grid[[paste(i)]] <- tibble(m = grid$m_values[i], 
                                   learning_rate = grid$lr_values[i], 
                                   #filters = grid$filters[i], 
                                   epochs = grid$epochs[i], 
                                   batch_size = grid$batch_size[i], 
                                   balanced_accuracy = snn)
    }
  bind_rows(snn_grid) # final results
}

```

```{r}
#| label: snn-hpo-format

# Function to format table
table_form <- function(results_to_format) {
  results_to_format %>% 
    select(m, learning_rate, batch_size, balanced_accuracy) %>% 
    arrange(desc(balanced_accuracy)) %>%
    mutate(learning_rate = format(learning_rate, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE),
           across(balanced_accuracy, ~ 100 * .x)) %>%
    select(m, learning_rate, batch_size, balanced_accuracy) %>%
    head(10) %>%
    kable(col.names = c("Margin", "Learning rate", "Batch size", "Validation balanced accuracy (%)"),
          digits = 1, align = "r")
}
  
# Function to format figures
figure_form <- function(results_to_format) {
  
  results_to_format %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = learning_rate, y = balanced_accuracy, colour = factor(m))) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = unique(results_to_format$learning_rate)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    facet_wrap(~ batch_size, labeller = labeller(batch_size = function(f) paste("Batch size:", f))) +
    labs(x = "Learning rate", y = "Balanced accuracy (validation)", colour = "Margin:") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
}
```


Once again, learning rate had the largest effect on balanced accuracy (@fig-snn-hpo-coarse). Averaged across the other two hyperparameters, balanced accuracy fell from `r snn_hpo_coarse_lr$balanced_accuracy[3]`% at a learning rate of 0.01 to `r snn_hpo_coarse_lr$balanced_accuracy[1]`% at 0.0001. Both the margin (`r snn_hpo_coarse_m$balanced_accuracy[4]`% at $m = 2$ up to `r snn_hpo_coarse_m$balanced_accuracy[1]`% at $m = 0.5$) and the batch size (`r snn_hpo_coarse_batch_size$balanced_accuracy[3]`% at a batch size of 128, compared with `r snn_hpo_coarse_batch_size$balanced_accuracy[1]`% at 32) had smaller effects on balanced accuracy. The best-performing learning rate and margin were at the edge of the coarse grid (@fig-snn-hpo-coarse), so the refined grid extended the ranges of both variables and fixed the batch size at 32 (@fig-snn-hpo-refined). The number of epochs was fixed at 5 across both grids.

The model was retrained on the training data using the selected hyperparameters and was evaluated on the test set. Balanced accuracy was calculated overall, by digit (@tbl-snn-hpo-test-digits), and by whether the image pairs came from the same or different sessions (@tbl-snn-hpo-test-sessions). Interestingly, the test balanced accuracy was higher than the validation accuracy. This is likely due to different writers having different levels of variability in their handwriting style and the limited test and validation sets each only containing four writers. The test set may have had writers whose handwriting styles were more distinguishable from each others than the writers in the validation set. Overall, the tuned model achieved higher test balanced accuracy than that of the initial model. 

```{r}
#| label: snn-hpo-test-model
#| eval: !expr snn_hpo_run_predict

# Optimal hyperparameters
m = snn_best_refined$m
learning_rate = snn_best_refined$learning_rate
epochs = snn_best_refined$epochs
batch_size = snn_best_refined$batch_size

# Fit model using these hyperparameters
image <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1)) # each image = 28x28, 1 image channel

z <- image |>
  layer_conv_2d(16, kernel_size = c(3,3), activation = "relu") |> # learns useful features (shapes, strokes)
  layer_max_pooling_2d(2) |> # makes feature maps smaller while keeping important info
  layer_conv_2d(32, kernel_size = c(3,3), activation = "relu") |>
  layer_global_average_pooling_2d() |> # converts feature maps -> single vector of numbers
  layer_dense(16) # converts to 16-no embedding representing the handwriting style

encoder <- keras_model(image, z)

a <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))
b <- layer_input(shape = c(28, 28, 1))

distance <- list(encoder(a), encoder(b)) |>
  layer_lambda(f = function(z) {
    op_sqrt(op_sum(op_square(z[[1]] - z[[2]]), 
                   axis = 2, # sum over embedding dimension
                   keepdims = TRUE) + 
              1e-7) # makes sure it's not 0
  })

model <- keras_model(list(a, b), distance)

contrastive_loss <- function(y, d) {
  op_mean( # finds avg loss across all pairs in a batch
    y * op_square(d) + # squares each pair's distance - for same-writer pairs, penalises a large distance
      (1 - y) * op_square(op_maximum(m - d, 0))) # for diff writer pairs, penalises only if distance is < 1: if dist >=1, penalty is 0
}

set_random_seed(25)

model |> compile(
  optimizer = optimizer_adam(learning_rate = learning_rate),
  loss = contrastive_loss
)

model |> fit(
  list(train$left, train$right), train$y,
  validation_data = list(
    list(valid$left, valid$right), valid$y
  ),
  epochs = epochs,
  batch_size = batch_size,
  verbose=0
)

# Calculate the model predicted distances between the pairs in the validation data
valid_distance <- as.numeric(predict(model, list(valid$left, valid$right), verbose = 0))

# Calculate the model predicted distances between the pairs in the test data
test_distance <- as.numeric(predict(model, list(test$left, test$right), verbose = 0))

saveRDS(valid_distance, snn_hpo_validation_file)
saveRDS(test_distance, snn_hpo_test_file)

```

```{r}
#| label: snn-hpo-test

# Read in predictions on validation
valid_distance <- readRDS(snn_hpo_validation_file)
valid_same <- as.logical(valid$y[, 1])

threshold_candidates <- sort(unique(valid_distance))
threshold_scores <- vapply(threshold_candidates, balanced_accuracy_at, distance = valid_distance, same = valid_same, numeric(1))
best_index <- which.max(threshold_scores)
threshold <- threshold_candidates[best_index]
balanced_accuracy <- threshold_scores[best_index]

# Read in predictions on test
test_distance <- readRDS(snn_hpo_test_file)
# Extract the observed labels for whether the pairs are the same or different for test data
true_same <- as.logical(test$y[, 1]) 

# Calculate balanced accuracy on test set
snn_hpo_test_results <- balanced_accuracy_at(distance = test_distance, same = true_same, cut = threshold)

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-snn-hpo-test-digits
#| tbl-cap: "Balanced accuracy for tuned Siamese neural network predictions on pairs of images in the test set including a breakdown of balanced accuracy by digit."

# Break down balanced accuracy by digit
# Set up tibble for results with the first row the combined balanced accuracy
snn_hpo_test_results_table_digits <- tibble(Digit = "All digits", 
                                            Images = length(true_same), 
                                            Balanced_accuracy = snn_hpo_test_results)

# Find the digit used in each pair in test_pairs
test_digits <- tibble(image_id = test_pairs[, 1]) %>% 
  left_join(handwriting$metadata) %>% 
  select(digit) %>% pull()

# Add digit to tibble with true and predicted same or different
test_digits_df <- tibble(true_same = true_same,
                         test_distance = test_distance,
                         test_digits = test_digits)

# Loop over each digit and calculate metrics for each then append row to results table
for (i in 0:4) {
  
  test_digits_df_temp <- test_digits_df %>% filter(test_digits == i)
  
  snn_hpo_test_results_digits_loop <- balanced_accuracy_at(distance = test_digits_df_temp$test_distance, 
                                                           same = test_digits_df_temp$true_same, 
                                                           cut = threshold)
  
  snn_hpo_test_results_table_digits <- snn_hpo_test_results_table_digits %>% add_row(Digit = as.character(i), Images = nrow(test_digits_df_temp), Balanced_accuracy = snn_hpo_test_results_digits_loop)
  
}

snn_hpo_test_results_table_digits %>%
  mutate(across(c(Balanced_accuracy), ~ 100 * .x)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Balanced_accuracy)) %>%
  arrange(Digit == "All digits") %>%
  kable(digits = 1, align = "r", col.names = c("Digit", "Image pairs", "Test balanced accuracy (%)"))

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-snn-hpo-test-sessions
#| tbl-cap: "Balanced accuracy for tuned Siamese neural network predictions on pairs of images in the test set including a breakdown of balanced accuracy for digits in the same and in different sessions."

# Break down balanced accuracy by session
# Set up tibble for results with the first row the combined balanced accuracy
snn_hpo_test_results_table_sessions <- tibble(Session = "All sessions", 
                                              Images = length(true_same), 
                                              Balanced_accuracy = snn_hpo_test_results)

# Find the session used in each pair in test_pairs for both left and right images
test_session_left <- tibble(image_id = test_pairs[, 1]) %>% 
  left_join(handwriting$metadata) %>% 
  select(session) %>% pull()

test_session_right <- tibble(image_id = test_pairs[, 2]) %>% 
  left_join(handwriting$metadata) %>% 
  select(session) %>% pull()

# Add digit to tibble with true and predicted same or different
test_session_df <- tibble(true_same = true_same,
                         test_distance = test_distance,
                         # session the same or different 
                         test_session = factor(x = test_session_left == test_session_right, 
                                               levels = c(TRUE, FALSE), 
                                               labels = c("Same session", "Different session"))) # change to named factor

# Loop over each digit and calculate metrics for each then append row to results table
for (i in c("Same session", "Different session")) {
  
  test_session_df_temp <- test_session_df %>% filter(test_session == i)
  
  snn_hpo_test_results_sessions_loop <- balanced_accuracy_at(distance = test_session_df_temp$test_distance, 
                                           same = test_session_df_temp$true_same, 
                                           cut = threshold)
  
  snn_hpo_test_results_table_sessions <- snn_hpo_test_results_table_sessions %>% add_row(Session = as.character(i), Images = nrow(test_session_df_temp), Balanced_accuracy = snn_hpo_test_results_sessions_loop)
  
}

snn_hpo_test_results_table_sessions %>%
  mutate(across(c(Balanced_accuracy), ~ 100 * .x)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Balanced_accuracy)) %>%
  arrange(Session == "All sessions") %>%
  kable(digits = 1, align = "r", col.names = c("Session", "Image pairs", "Test balanced accuracy (%)"))


```
